messages:
From: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@atlashealth.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 May 2027 09:18:00 -0700
Subject: Reserved capacity ask + guardrail question

Marcus — thanks again for the demo last week. Atlas is preparing a 12‑month pilot and we expect bursty QPS across models (NLP + embedding heavy). Procurement asked me to confirm two things before we proceed to a term sheet: 1) can Redwood offer a pricing guardrail if spot GPU costs spike, and 2) what discount band you can commit to for a 12‑month reserved bucket if we sign this month?

Attaching our expected consumption profile separately. High level: 3M tokens/mo baseline, peaks to 9M tokens/mo for short windows. We prefer a predictable monthly charge.

— Sarah
VP Engineering, Atlas Health

---
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sarah Jones <sarah.jones@atlashealth.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Wed, 26 May 2027 10:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + guardrail question

Sarah — great to hear the pilot is moving forward. Quick summary of a pragmatic structure we can offer:

- Reservation tenor: 12 months with monthly billing and a 30% headroom bucket for burst capacity.
- Pricing hedge (what we internally call "capacity insurance"): an optional monthly surcharge (0.5%–1.5% of committed spend) that buys a floor protection. If GPU market spot costs increase >15% quarter‑over‑quarter, we cap your per‑token uplift to a predefined pass‑through of +8% (instead of full market uplift). This is intended to stabilize unit economics for you while sharing limited upside with Redwood.
- Discount band: for a 12‑month reserved SKU mix aligned to your profile, we can start at 12% standard discount off list with the ability to stretch to 18% with exec authorization, tied to minimum monthly commit and a small non‑refundable onboarding credit.

I attached a SKU matrix with proposed reserved buckets and estimated monthly billing (atlas_reserve_sku_matrix_v2.xlsx). Please review and tell me which bucket you expect to sign for.

If acceptable I will route for internal finance/legal approval and propose the amendment language for the pricing hedge.

— Marcus
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: internal: Atlas pricing hedge — approval path and guardrails

Looping finance. A few things we need to lock down before we offer an 18% stretch:

1) Minimum monthly committed spend threshold (proposed $65k/mo). Below that we revert to 12% discount and no hedge.
2) Deferral / escape triggers — market passthrough capped to +8% for the customer when insured, but Redwood must retain a right to negotiate if GPU hourly spot >250% baseline for two consecutive months.
3) SKU mix binding — discount applies only to the reserved SKUs mapped in the attached matrix, not ad‑hoc burst instances.

Marissa — anything to add from capacity planning/ops? I want to make sure this is operationally feasible (we're not over‑allocating GPUs we can't spin up).

— Karthik
Director, Sales Ops

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 27 May 2027 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: internal: Atlas pricing hedge — approval path and guardrails

Karthik — operational notes from capacity planning:

- The 30% headroom is fine if we reserve a mix that skews toward longer‑running inference shapes (higher batch efficiency). We should lock their reserved SKUs for the quarter and allow burst into a shared pool subject to quorum limits.
- If we provide the hedge, we should add a one‑time "capacity insurance" technical onboarding to validate token distributions — two days of SRE onboarding billed to the customer. This prevents abuse and ensures KV cache efficiency.
- Capacity wise, we can meet the proposed baseline but we'll need a 6‑week lead time for contracted expansion beyond 40% of their initial reserved footprint. Add this to the amendment.

Marissa
Head of Capacity Planning

From: Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal — Contracts <legal_contracts@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 28 May 2027 09:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: internal: Atlas pricing hedge — approval path and guardrails

Finance perspective / required guardrails:

- Approval threshold: any discount >15% requires SVP sign‑off; >18% requires CFO sign‑off. Recommend we put the 18% stretch behind a one‑time credit hold and a clause that links the hedge to documented monthly consumption and SKU adherence.
- Accounting: the insurance surcharge needs to be treated as a separate revenue line and deferred over contract life; ops must pass billing events to revenue ops.
- Risk: we should add a bilateral true‑up at quarter close if Atlas’ actual usage deviates >25% from forecast. This protects Redwood from systematic under‑forecasting.

I will draft the amendment language and circulate redlines (see draft_amendment_redlines.pdf). Legal: please review the passthrough trigger language and the escape clause.

— Neha
Head of Revenue Ops & FP&A

Date: Mon, 30 May 2027 15:42:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Reserved capacity ask + guardrail question

Sarah — thanks for the patience. Per internal review the commercial path is:

- Standard offer: 12% discount on the reserved SKU mix; 30% burst headroom; 12‑month term.
- Optional capacity insurance: 0.75% monthly surcharge to cap customer passthrough to +8% in event of GPU market increases >15% QoQ.
- Stretch discount: up to 18% available with conditions (commit >= $65k/mo, one‑time onboarding credit, and SVP approval).

If this aligns with Atlas' procurement constraints, I'm ready to push draft amendment to DocuSign. Next steps: confirm target SKU bucket and which billing account to use.

Sarah replied (separate thread) that procurement is comfortable with the structure and asked us to issue the DocuSign with the 12% baseline and the 18% clause included as an "executive exception" to be filled if approvals arrive within 14 days of signing.

Attachments: atlas_reserve_sku_matrix_v2.xlsx (reserved SKU map), draft_amendment_redlines.pdf (legal redlines).

— Marcus
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
